Wow, so much to talk about on the truck...

So last update, I talked about how I started ripping out the camper section. Truth be told, it's been too hot and humid to spend a lot of time working on it but this last week has been busy...

I usually work with a buddy since more hands make for lighter work but I was getting anxious and I knew that I could get some of these things done myself. So this last week:

  1. I took the water tank out. The dipshit that built this didn't even bolt the damned thing down! He just had 4 bent pieces of metal bolted to the metal floor of the truck bed. Nothing holding down! That means that tipping and rocking could and would have tipped the tank over. Fucking hell...

  2. I managed to get the water tank (picture those big square ones with the metal cage and a plastic pallet) to the end of the bed and emptied it out. Slid that onto the trailer for my riding lawn mower and toted that to the external garage. In the process, the valve came out. Fucking hell, that dipshit did not use PVC glue, just some stupid ass gel style glue that falls apart with age. So now I have a 300 gallon tank that I'm going to install in the garage as a water collection unit :)

  3. During this process, I discovered that the extra diesel tank is half full. Remember, this is one of those older heating oil tanks. It's not air tight and has a hand pump on top. Not only is it half full, the fucking idiot that put it in only bolted it down on one side and only sunk bolts into the metal plating for the floor. Not nuts or anything to keep it from pulling out. Jesus fuck, this guy. I mean, I knew I'd be rebuilding the whole thing but fucking hell...

  4. Since there's fuel in the tank, I need to store it somewhere. Scored two 55 gallon drums for free. Got at some local plastic company, they said "Take as many as you want." Fuck yes. I grabbed two but it has some oil based white greasy crap all over it. No toxicity apparently so that's good. I'm gonna do some research but if it's oil based like I think, some mineral spirits and a bunch of swishing should take care of all that I need it to do. Got those today.

  5. Took the solar panels off today too. They were stopping me from ripping out the rest of the inside since the wires were fed through a wall. See, I have to take the ceiling down first, then the floor, then the walls. These wires were up in a corner and if I ripped the ceiling down, it would cut the wires. Fine. My buddy was on top of the camper while I was inside. He used a socket wrench to hold the bolt while I took the screwdriver/drill and pull the nuts off. I now have two disconnected solar panels, 18 volts each at 100 watts each. Sitting in my garage. I might just temporarily set those up with the inverter and batteries for emergencies should one happen while I'm building.

  6. So now that that's all done, I can finish ripping the plywood panels off and pry up the floor. That'll start happening this week as I get time after work.

So what's next?

Aside from ripping out the inside panels, I have to take a shelf out. A shelf the size of a bed. The problem is that there's a plastic cabinet wedged between it and the ceiling and there's been enough ceiling sag to make it all but impossible to just yank out. After the shelf is out (which I may reuse, I don't know), I'll be ripping the water collection pipes out and capping those until I'm ready to actually redo them. Oh, and it turns out that this yahoo moron built the top of the camper so that it is basically a stagnant water trap. Yeah, that's going to change.

Once all of that is out, I'll post pictures of the inside. I'll probably also pull the plywood off of the "cargo style" doors on the back and replace it with metal. Thinner, lighter, stronger. I figure I'm also going to build a solar heater out of soda cans :) No freezing in the winter for me.

After that, I have to pull out the ceiling 2x4s and replace them with 4x4s which won't sag. Pop some new high quality plywood on for the roof and then coat with Pond Armor. Waterproof that shit and non-toxic. Water collection will rock. Ceiling will be secure and stable. Ceiling will be 100% waterproof. And I'll install some ceiling lights while I'm at it. My buddy keeps talking about an acrylic window panels in the ceiling to let sunlight in. Not sure it's a good idea but, meh, I'll consider that. Actually, I like the idea of lots of smaller windows... but we'll see.

And I guess after that, the side panels. That should be a lot easier. I figure some thin but high quality plywood or sheet metal. Killz the shit out of it, put it up, seal it with a sealant of some kind. No rust. Lighter. Paint the inside whatever the fuck color I want.
Damn, that's a lot. I applaud you for taking on such a big project.

Thanks. I mean, I know I would be rebuilding it when I bought it. The thing I was looking for was a vehicle that would go anywhere and I wouldn't have to prep completely from scratch. So far, the walls on the camper look solid (plus), the solar system is a go (plus), the vehicle runs on anything (plus). It's worth it to me.

Besides, I've historically sucked when it comes to power tools and vehicle repair. It's time to fix that.
